extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners, patent owners, third-party petitioners, and USPTO rulemaking stakeholders
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and regulatory standards implementing the America Invents Act (AIA) procedures for inter partes review, post-grant review, covered business method review, and related information-collection and Executive Order compliance. Focuses on procedural requirements, burden estimation, and policy considerations for initiating and conducting review proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of rule effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess the effect of the rules on the economy, the integrity of the patent system, the efficient administration of the Office, and the ability of the Office to complete the instituted proceedings timely.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulatory decisions should weigh economic impacts, system integrity, USPTO administrative efficiency, and timeliness of proceedings; balance burdens against objectives when adopting filing systems or other procedural rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flexibility in electronic filing authorization
rubrics_metrics.description: Entity size and sophistication should be considered in determining whether alternative filing methods would be authorized rather than rigidly applying an electronic-only filing requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A rigid electronic-only filing system may impose unnecessary costs and burdens on parties lacking ability to file electronically; the Office will consider alternatives for less-sophisticated or small entities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify duplicative/overlapping/conflicting federal rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify, to the extent practicable, all relevant Federal rules which may duplicate, overlap, or conflict with the final rules (e.g., 37 CFR 1.99, 1.171-1.179, 1.291, 1.321, 1.501-1.502, 1.902-1.997).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Catalog existing regulations that involve patent applications and patents and explain where processes overlap or differ (for example, reissue, protest, disclaimer, reexamination provisions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Inter partes reexamination procedural differences
rubrics_metrics.description: Inter partes reexamination provides a different threshold for initiation, requires proceedings to be conducted by an examiner with a right of appeal to the PTAB, and allows limited third-party participation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain how inter partes reexamination differs from the new AIA proceedings and how those differences affect initiation, participation, and appeal rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elimination of inter partes reexamination practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Inter partes reexamination practice will be eliminated except for requests filed before the effective date (September 16, 2012) per AIA §6(c)(3)(C).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe transitional handling of pre-effective-date requests and the expected offsetting burden reductions from eliminating the practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Executive Order 12866 significance threshold
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine whether rulemaking is 'significant' for EO 12866 and whether it is 'economically significant' (economic significance defined as $100,000,000 or more annual effect).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use OMB designations and economic thresholds when classifying regulatory significance; present cost estimates to support the determination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Burden estimation methodology - baseline and offsets
rubrics_metrics.description: Estimate aggregate burden by including baseline burdens that existed before the statutory change and offsetting burdens eliminated (e.g., elimination of inter partes reexamination).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use historical filing and outcome data, average cost estimates (AIPLA Report), grant rates, and appeal rates to calculate net burden; follow OMB Circular A4 guidance for baselines and offsets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of historical filing and grant data in cost estimates
rubrics_metrics.description: Use historical filing counts (e.g., FY 2009-2011) and expected filing rates (e.g., estimated 456 annual inter partes reexamination filings) and grant rates (e.g., 93%) to project costs and offsets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Base estimates on recent years' filing patterns and observed grant/appeal rates to approximate avoided burdens and filing-fee offsets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Targeted Board final-determination timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to 35 U.S.C. 316(a) and 326(a), the Director must prescribe regulations requiring a final determination by the Board within one year of initiation, with a possible six-month extension for good cause.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt timelines significantly shorter than prior reexamination averages (e.g., 28.9–41.7 months) to reduce review time; allow extensions only for good cause.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordination with district court litigation and filing timeliness (35 U.S.C. 315(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Require that a petition for inter partes review be filed within one year of the date of service of a complaint alleging infringement to reduce duplication with litigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Earlier filing requirements and shorter USPTO timelines aim to reduce overlap between USPTO review and district-court validity determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of external economic data (AIPLA Report and litigation costs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Incorporate external estimates of litigation costs and damages-risk buckets (AIPLA Report) when evaluating potential reductions in overall burden and litigation overlap.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use reasonable external surveys and court statistics to assess cost impacts and potential savings from coordinated procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Executive Order 13563 compliance elements
rubrics_metrics.description: To the extent feasible, the rulemaking must: (1) make a reasoned determination that benefits justify costs; (2) tailor the rule to impose the least burden consistent with objectives; (3) select an approach that maximizes net benefits; (4) specify performance objectives; (5) identify and assess alternatives; (6) involve the public and provide online docket access; (7) promote coordination, simplification, harmonization, and innovation; (8) consider approaches that reduce burdens and maintain flexibility; and (9) ensure objectivity of scientific and technological information and processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document how each element is addressed in the rulemaking record; provide evidence of public involvement, alternatives analysis, cost–benefit reasoning, and safeguards for objectivity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Executive Order 13132 federalism consideration
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether rulemaking contains policies with federalism implications sufficient to warrant a Federalism Assessment; if not, no assessment required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State the conclusion and basis (e.g., no substantial direct effects on states) when federalism implications are absent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Executive Order 13175 tribal consultation assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine whether rulemaking will have substantial direct effects on Indian tribes, impose substantial direct costs on tribal governments, or preempt tribal law; if not, tribal summary impact statement not required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain why the rule does or does not trigger tribal-consultation obligations under EO 13175.

rubrics_metrics.name: Executive Order 13211 energy effects consideration
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate whether the rule is a 'significant energy action' likely to have a significant adverse effect on supply, distribution, or use of energy; if not, a Statement of Energy Effects is not required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document analysis concluding absence of significant energy impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Executive Order 12988 civil justice reform standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure the rule meets standards to minimize litigation, eliminate ambiguity, and reduce burden as set forth in EO 12988.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Draft clear, unambiguous regulatory text and procedures designed to lessen litigation where statute permits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paperwork Reduction Act information-collection requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify information collections added to OMB control number 0651–0069, including petitions to institute inter partes review, post-grant review, covered business method review; motions, oppositions, replies; notices of judicial review; requests for oral argument, rehearing, adverse judgment, settlement confidentiality; and other related submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide title, description, respondent categories, estimated responses, hours per response, and estimated costs; submit revisions to OMB for approval and publish the information-collection details for public review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Estimated time and cost per response and aggregate burden reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide estimates of time per response (range 0.1–165.3 hours), estimated total annual respondent burden hours, total annual (hour) respondent cost burden (using $371/hour attorney rate), and total annual non-hour respondent cost burden (filing fees, postage).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Break down estimates by filing type (petitions, replies, motions, requests) with proposed and final estimated annual responses, hours, and fees; include assumptions (e.g., mail via EXPRESS MAIL®) and justify rates used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition preparation cost assumptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Estimate cost to prepare a petition for inter partes review by referencing inter partes reexamination preparation cost ($46,000) and increasing by 33.333% for additional grounds in post-grant review, yielding $61,333 for a petition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document basis for percentage increase and reliance on historical preparation costs; adjust where additional grounds increase preparation time and costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Weighting factors for estimated proceeding costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Estimate inter partes review cost at 60% of current contested Board cases to the end of preliminary motion period; estimate post-grant review and covered business method review cost at 75% of current contested Board cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Justify weighting based on expected fewer motions, absence of priority issues, and overlapping costs spread over fewer motions; use Board contested-case data to calibrate percentages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excess claims fee and small-entity adjustments
rubrics_metrics.description: Estimate the percentage of proceedings presenting excess claims and the proportion of patent owners paying small-entity fees; calculate expected additional claim-fee revenue (example: estimated total excess claim fee $49,580 in FY2013).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use historical data for inter partes reexamination to estimate excess-claim presentation rates and small-entity election rates; apply statutory fee amounts (35 U.S.C. 41(a)(2)(i)-(ii)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Settlement paperwork burden estimates and adjustment
rubrics_metrics.description: Estimate burden for submitting settlement information: increase burden to 100 hours per settlement for inter partes and post-grant proceedings where parties are not concurrently in district-court litigation (adopted after comment); note statutory requirement that covered business-method petitioners be in litigation or charged with infringement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt higher settlement-submission burden where historical evidence suggests prior estimate was too low; state fraction of reviewed patents expected not to be in concurrent litigation (e.g., 30%).

rubrics_metrics.name: Uses of information collections by the USPTO
rubrics_metrics.description: The information supplied by petitions and authorized motions is used by the USPTO to determine whether to initiate reviews (under 35 U.S.C. 314, 324, or derivation under 135) and to prepare final decisions under the applicable statutory sections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe how collected information supports initiation, institution decisions, and preparation of final agency decisions; include reference to the relevant statutory bases.
